$comment: PATTERN STUDY — designed 2026-08-14, to be measured on the Monday session.
WHY THIS EXISTS. The 28-day Search Console report to 2026-08-12 shows 101 clicks
on 35,200 impressions, and the click-through rate is flat across positions:
0.30% at positions 6-10 (22,852 impressions) against 0.31% at positions 11-20
(10,273). Ranking does not buy clicks here, so the question moved to what does.
WHY BY PATTERN AND NOT BY QUERY. The query table lists 1000 queries totalling
3300 impressions and 5 clicks — 9% of impressions and 5% of clicks. The other
91% sits in the anonymised tail, and the largest single query has 55 impressions.
There is no head to measure. Queries here are therefore samples of a TEMPLATE,
and the finding we want generalises to the template, not to the instance.
THE HYPOTHESIS, WRITTEN BEFORE MEASURING so it can actually be wrong: a query
asking for one exact clock time gets answered by the AI Overview and yields no
click; a query asking for a direction, a table, or a span leaves something for
the result to supply and does get clicks. The aggregate that suggested it is thin
and is stated as such below.
PREDICTIONS, one per pattern, recorded now:
A, B, D, E -> AI Overview present AND stating the time. Expect no click.
F, G       -> no AI Overview, or one that does not answer. Expect clicks.
C (German) -> AI Overview less often than the Spanish and English equivalents.
If A/B/D/E and F/G come out the same, the hypothesis is dead and the CTR ceiling
is not about query shape at all.
BUDGET CONFLICT, resolved by the owner on 2026-08-14: run both sets rather than
skip either. The Monday reminder (.github/workflows/experiment-guard.yml) asks
for the 10 fixed queries of queries.json, and the agreed cadence was 10 a week.
Split into two sessions on different days instead of one 20-query sitting: this
set on 08-14, the fixed series on 08-17. That keeps the per-session limit — the
half of the rule that actually protects the account — and relaxes only the weekly
frequency. Spacing from the 08-10 baseline is 4 days, then 3.
METHOD, carrying the two traps the baseline hit plus the gaps it recorded:
- Owner's profiled Chrome only. 10 queries, >=15s apart, hard stop on the
first block. Do not probe for the rate limit.
- Decide 'cited' by geometry (link top vs overview block bottom), never by DOM
containment — that gave a false positive at 2088px in the baseline.
- Record aioCitedDomains (inside the overview's source box) SEPARATELY from
page-wide topDomains. The baseline conflated them and says so.
- Keep a screenshot per query keyed by id. The baseline kept none, so its rows
can only be re-measured, never re-audited.
- One reading per query is noisy: the baseline saw us organically on 08-09 and
gone on 08-10 for the same query. Single rows are not trends.
FIELDS TO CAPTURE PER QUERY: aiOverview, aioAnswersTheQuestion (does it state the
clock time outright), aioBottomPx, firstOrganicTopPx, viewportPx, present,
ourTopPx, aioCitedDomains[], topDomains[], peopleAlsoAsk, blocked.
